vehicles.summary: Audited 2026 RAV4 Hybrid guide: six grades and nine FWD/AWD configurations. Brochure Standard/Available marks are preserved; published maximum torque and HEV-only applicability are clarified. Unresolved ratings and unexplained equipment blanks retain specific audit reasons.

sources.title: Toyota 2026 RAV4 brochure — supplied PDF, 30 pages; HEV grade/equipment tables pp. 17–25, package caveat p. 30
sources.scope: HEV tables only. Manufacturer link is the official model page, not a claim that this PDF was downloaded from that URL. Data-quality audit rechecked every previously Unverified HEV cell; maximum torque is quoted with unspecified basis. Plug-in-specific fields are classified not applicable to HEV, not inferred from blank matrix entries.

gains.text: Within HEV: gain 18-inch wheels, SofTex, an 8-way power driver seat, heated front seats and a power liftgate; add one wireless charger and front/rear Parking Assist with Automatic Braking.
FWD remains available. For AWD, listed towing capacity rises from 1,750 lb (LE) to 3,500 lb when properly equipped.
Limited is AWD-only. Gain a panoramic glass roof, hands-free liftgate, 12.9-inch screen and 9-speaker JBL audio.
Gain front-seat ventilation, heated rear outboard seats, power passenger seat, driver memory, heated steering wheel, two wireless chargers, 3D Panoramic View Monitor and Advanced Park.
XSE Hybrid is AWD-only. Gain 20-inch wheels, a moonroof, hands-free liftgate, Ultrasuede/SofTex and an 8-way power passenger seat with driver-seat memory.

XSE lists front-seat ventilation, a 12.9-inch screen, one wireless charger, 3D Panoramic View Monitor, Lane Change Assist and Front Cross-Traffic Alert as standard; unexplained SE table blanks do not prove those features are unavailable. Traffic Jam Assist requires active Drive Connect.

Choose a rugged HEV AWD alternative: all-terrain tires, raised rails/crossbars, 2-inch hitch with wiring, 8.5-inch ground clearance, LED fog lights, SofTex, heated steering wheel, all-weather mats and standard cargo AC outlet. This is a change of emphasis, not a claim that every SE feature carries over.

notes: The supplied Toyota 2026 RAV4 brochure verifies HEV equipment/optional marks and package names (pp. 17–25); the Toyota 2026 release verifies the HEV/PHEV configuration matrix and the explicitly named PHEV grade equipment. Verification is claim-specific, not a claim that every cell is known.

Data-quality audit: all 93 previously Unverified HEV equipment cells were individually checked. Nine torque cells now report the brochure’s explicit 170 lb-ft maximum with its unspecified basis. Twenty-seven plug-in-specific range/charging cells are classified Unavailable / not applicable to conventional HEV. Fifty-seven cells remain Unverified for the documented reasons in the audit; unexplained matrix blanks are not automatically negative availability claims.

Torque provenance: the brochure’s maximum is reported verbatim, not as a confirmed combined-system or engine-only figure. No engine/motor torque is added. Fuel economy and FWD towing still require accessible, configuration-specific official records; failed Toyota/EPA reads are not evidence that no published rating exists.

Fuel economy: the release conflicts internally. HEV FWD is described as up to 41, 43 and 44 combined mpg; XSE/Limited HEV are listed with 41 or 42 combined mpg and one inconsistent city/highway set. Woodland PHEV is given as 37 or 38 combined mpg; GR SPORT as 36 or 37. Unresolved MPG cells remain Unverified rather than selecting a convenient number. Woodland HEV and SE/XSE PHEV figures shown are manufacturer estimates, not verified EPA results.

The brochure names eight HEV package offerings and their grade eligibility, but does not itemize package contents. Package names are verified; contents, combinations and pricing remain Unverified. Its equipment tables mark S=Standard and A=Available; unexplained blank cells are treated as Unverified, not proof of Unavailable. PHEV packages are not verified by this HEV brochure.

The supplied brochure’s six-grade equipment tables cover HEV only; they do not verify PHEV/GR SPORT availability or packages. It does not resolve conflicting MPG in the release, provide a verified EPA fuel-economy table, clarify torque basis, or confirm total seating capacity, PHEV transmission type, or FWD/GR SPORT towing limits.

Confirm actual equipment and installed packages against the window sticker. Observe vehicle-specific towing/loading limits and charging requirements. Driver assistance is not autonomous driving; subscriptions, road and weather conditions apply.

gains.text: Within PHEV AWD: gain an 11-kW AC charger, CCS1 port and DC fast charging instead of the SE’s 7-kW/J1772 AC-only arrangement.

Gain 20-inch wheels, moonroof, hands-free liftgate, Ultrasuede/SofTex with power front seats and driver memory, front-seat ventilation, 12.9-inch screen and 3D Panoramic View Monitor. Head-up display and cargo outlet are optional; packages unverified.

Choose a rugged PHEV AWD alternative with all-terrain tires, hitch/wiring, raised rails/crossbars, heated steering wheel and cargo AC outlet. Gain 11-kW/CCS1 DC charging; manufacturer-estimated EV range changes from 52 to 49 miles. Named packages and conflicting Woodland MPG remain unverified.
Choose the handling-focused PHEV AWD: GR-tuned suspension/steering, functional aero, 20-inch wheels, bolstered Brin Naub/SofTex sport seats, heated steering wheel and 12.9-inch screen.
GR SPORT retains 7-kW/J1772 AC-only charging; it does not gain XSE/Woodland DC charging. Manufacturer-estimated EV range is 48 miles. Do not treat GR SPORT as a universal equipment upgrade over XSE.

notes: Detailed PHEV specifications and package contents are awaiting separate documentation. The supplied 30-page RAV4 brochure equipment matrix covers six HEV grades, not these PHEV configurations. No HEV brochure equipment or packages have been copied here.
Only claims expressly supported by Toyota’s 2026 release are recorded. Missing fields remain Unverified; known release details do not make this a complete PHEV equipment guide.

The release conflicts on Woodland PHEV MPG (37 or 38 combined) and GR SPORT MPG (36 or 37 combined); those MPG cells remain Unverified. Displayed SE/XSE MPG and PHEV electric ranges are manufacturer estimates, not verified EPA ratings.

All four PHEVs are AWD with 324 net combined system hp. The 172 lb-ft figure is gasoline-engine-only. SE/GR SPORT use 7-kW/J1772 AC-only charging; XSE/Woodland use 11-kW/CCS1 with DC capability. Actual charging time and range vary.
Source-specific equipment and optional items are not a factory-package manifest. Confirm the actual vehicle window sticker and owner’s manual. Driver supervision and subscription conditions apply.
